Grafana dashboards, datasources, and alerting are managed from this folder and deployed by `azure-pipelines-docker.yml`.

## Structure

- `dashboards/`
  Grafana dashboard JSON files. Sub-folders become Grafana folders (`foldersFromFilesStructure: true`), e.g. `dashboards/Games` → the *Games* folder.
  **`Home Assistant.json` and `Topology.json` are generated by `build_ha_dashboard.py` — do not hand-edit them.** Add new panels/containers/probes to the script and run `python grafanaDashboards/build_ha_dashboard.py` from the repo root, then commit both the script change and the regenerated JSON. A hand-edit to either file will be silently overwritten the next time someone (or another Claude session) reruns the generator without first folding your change into the script.
- `build_ha_dashboard.py`
  The generator for the two files above (the "Home Assistant" main dashboard, collapsed Topology/Stats rows, and the standalone `ha-topology` dashboard the Home Assistant Lovelace "Topology" view embeds).
- `mermaid-validate/`
  A Node script that parses every `jdbranham-diagram-panel`'s mermaid content against **mermaid 8.8.0 exactly** - the version that plugin's *published* build bundles (confirmed by downloading `jdbranham-diagram-panel-1.7.3.zip` from its GitHub release and grepping the minified `module.js`; the plugin's own `package.json` says `mermaid: ^8.8.0`, but that range resolves to whatever was newest 8.x when the plugin was built - frozen at 8.8.0 - not whatever `npm install mermaid@^8.8.0` gives you today). 8.8.0 predates several mermaid features a browser preview of a newer mermaid renders happily - most notably per-subgraph `direction`, which it parses as a bare vertex id and then fails on the next token, breaking the whole panel in Grafana with no warning until someone opens it. Run once per checkout: `cd grafanaDashboards/mermaid-validate && npm install`; then after any change to the diagram content in `build_ha_dashboard.py`, `node grafanaDashboards/mermaid-validate/validate.js` (the generator also runs this automatically at the end, when `node_modules` is present, and refuses to finish if a panel fails to parse).
- `provisioning/dashboards/`
  Grafana dashboard provider definitions.
- `provisioning/datasources/`
  Grafana datasource provisioning files.
- `provisioning/alerting/`
  Grafana alerting provisioning files (Grafana provisioning format, `apiVersion: 1`).
- `catalog/`
  Genericized dashboards authored/shared to the [grafana.com community catalog](https://grafana.com/grafana/dashboards) - **not** imported into this repo's Grafana (deliberately outside `dashboards/`, never provisioned). See `catalog/README.md`.
- `dashboard-index.json`
  Raw dashboard search export from the Grafana API.
- `folders.json`
  Raw folder export from the Grafana API.
- `datasources-export.json`
  Raw datasource export from the Grafana API.

The raw `*-export.json` files are snapshots from the live Grafana API, useful for diffing or regenerating provisioning later.

## Deployment flow

1. Commit dashboard JSON, datasource YAML, or alerting YAML into this folder **on `master`**. Branch pushes only build and validate the JSON — the `Deploy` stage of `azure-pipelines-docker.yml` triggers on `master` only (path filter `grafanaDashboards/*` + `grafanaDashboards/**/*`), so changes land via a PR merge.
2. The Docker pipeline validates every dashboard JSON (`json.load` on each file), packages this folder into the build artifact.
3. The `Deploy` job **wipes** `/home/homeassistant/.homeassistant/grafanaDashboards` on the host and re-copies it from the artifact, so the host is an exact mirror of the repo (see *Provisioning trap* below for why the wipe matters).
4. `docker-compose down && docker-compose up -d` restarts Grafana with these folders mounted read-only:
   - `.../grafanaDashboards/provisioning` → `/etc/grafana/provisioning`
   - `.../grafanaDashboards/dashboards` → `/var/lib/grafana/dashboards`
5. Grafana provisions datasources and alerting on boot, and the dashboard **file provider** (`provisioning/dashboards/dashboards.yml`) rescans `/var/lib/grafana/dashboards` every 30s.

Datasource secrets are **not** recoverable from the Grafana API. Any `__REPLACE_ME__` values in `provisioning/datasources/datasources.yml` must be filled before a clean reprovision on a new Grafana instance.

## How provisioning resolves dashboards

- Dashboard **identity is the JSON `uid`**. A file whose `uid` matches an existing dashboard updates it in place; the file's title/folder can change freely.
- `allowUiUpdates: true` — you can still edit provisioned dashboards in the UI, but a later change to the file wins.
- `disableDeletion: false` — deleting a file removes the dashboard from Grafana (which is why step 3 wipes-then-copies rather than just copying).

### Provisioning trap: duplicate uid / title jams *everything*

If the provisioned file set contains **any** duplicate `uid`, or two dashboards with the **same title in the same folder**, Grafana disables writes for the whole provider and logs:

```text
dashboards provisioning provider has no database write permissions because of duplicates
the same UID is used more than once   uid=<x> times=<n>
dashboard title is not unique in folder   title="<t>" folderID=<n>
```

Symptoms: repo edits stop appearing; `GET /api/dashboards/uid/<x>` shows `"provisioned": false` and a stale `version`.

Diagnose from Grafana's own logs in Loki:

```logql
{service_name="grafana"} |~ "provision"
```

Before adding or renaming a dashboard, check for collisions across `dashboards/**/*.json`:

```python
import json, glob, os, collections
uids, titles = collections.defaultdict(list), collections.defaultdict(list)
for p in glob.glob("dashboards/**/*.json", recursive=True):
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    uids[d.get("uid")].append(p)
    titles[(os.path.dirname(p), d.get("title"))].append(p)
for k, v in {**uids, **titles}.items():
    if len(v) > 1: print(k, v)
```

Historically this jammed because the old `Deploy` step only ever `cp`-ed dashboards onto the host and never pruned them, so every dashboard renamed or removed in git (`HomeAssistant old.json`, epoch-named exports like `HomeAssistant-1580940769856.json`, `Home Assistant Copy.json`, …) stayed on disk and collided. The wipe-then-copy in step 3 prevents this.

## Data sources

Grafana runs on the **LGTM stack** (containers in the repo-root `docker-compose.yml`). The old InfluxDB datasources (`000000001` HomeAssistant, `000000006` TelegrafStats, …) are dead — any dashboard still querying them shows *No data*.

| Datasource | uid | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mimir** (Prometheus) | `PAE45454D0EDB9216` | default. HA metrics scraped from `home-assistant:8123/api/prometheus`. |
| **Loki** | `P8E80F9AEF21F6940` | log streams keyed by `service_name` (`home-assistant`, `nginx_access`, `mimir`, `loki`, `adguard`, `unpoller`, …). |

### Home Assistant Prometheus metrics

Prefix `homeassistant_`, e.g. `homeassistant_sensor_temperature_celsius`, `homeassistant_sensor_power_w`,
`homeassistant_sensor_data_rate_mbit_per_s`, `homeassistant_sensor_unit_percent` (CPU / memory / disk %),
`homeassistant_binary_sensor_state`, `homeassistant_sensor_state`, `homeassistant_climate_*`.
Series carry `entity` (e.g. `sensor.speedtest_download`) and `friendly_name` labels.

### Blackbox exporter (topology diagrams)

The `blackbox` container powers the *Network Diagram* / *Cameras* panels (`dashboards/Home Assistant.json`) and
the `dashboards/Blackbox/` dashboards. Metrics: `probe_success`, `probe_duration_seconds`,
`probe_icmp_duration_seconds`, `probe_http_*`. The `instance` label is a friendly slug
(`hp_switch`, `server_1`, `firewall`, `google_dns`, `camera_front`, `u7_kitchen`, `grafana`, `mimir`, …);
`job` is `blackbox_icmp` / `blackbox_http` / `blackbox_tcp`.

## Annotations (deploy / system events)

Dashboards render Grafana-native annotations matched by tag (datasource `-- Grafana --`), toggled by the
`Deploy` / `System Events` switches on the "Home Assistant" dashboard:

| Source | Endpoint | Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `azure-pipelines.yml` / `azure-pipelines-docker.yml` deploy steps | `/api/annotations` (native - supports `time`/`timeEnd`) | One **region** annotation per deploy, posted once at the end covering the whole deploy span: `Deploy` + `HomeAssistant`/`Docker` (+ build number) |
| Host script `scripts/reboot_home_assistant.sh` | `/api/annotations/graphite` | `Reboot` |
| `scripts/home_assistant_service_started.sh` (called via `shell_command.home_assistant_service_started`) | `/api/annotations/graphite` | `Service` |
| `rest_command.grafana_annotation` (Restart Home Assistant / Reload YAML / Reload Lovelace / Clear IP ban list scripts) | `/api/annotations/graphite` | `Restart` / `Reload` / `Cleared IP Ban List` |

Both endpoints take an `Authorization: <grafana_api_key>` header (Bearer-prefixed for the native endpoint) at
`https://<host>:599/grafana`.

## PNG rendering

Panel/dashboard PNG rendering (alert images, scheduled reports, `get_panel_image`) is provided by a **remote
`grafana-image-renderer` sidecar** (`docker-compose.yml`), not the in-process plugin — the `grafana` container
is memory-capped. The `grafana` service points at it via
`GF_RENDERING_SERVER_URL=http://grafana-image-renderer:8081/render` and
`GF_RENDERING_CALLBACK_URL=http://grafana:3000/grafana/` (the callback keeps the `/grafana` sub-path because
`GF_SERVER_SERVE_FROM_SUB_PATH=true`).

## Alerting

Alerting files follow Grafana provisioning format with `apiVersion: 1` and live in `provisioning/alerting/`
(`contact-points.yml`, `policies.yml`, `alert-rules.yml`).
